title: Life in Biblical Israel
author: Philip J. King; Lawrence E. Stager
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted monograph. Summaries in project's own words only.
summary: Synthesis of Israelite daily life and material culture: houses and construction, dress and textiles, food production, water systems, tools, and household organization. Primary anchor for material-culture claims (mudbrick construction, dress, wells, household scale). The book's table of contents (independently corroborated across multiple published reviews) runs six chapters: an Israelite house/household chapter covering architecture, family, meals, and medicine; means-of-existence (farming, water, crafts, transport, trade); the patrimonial kingdom (royal city, water systems, warfare); culture and expressive life (dress, music, dance, literacy); and religious institutions, which includes a dedicated treatment of death, burial, and the afterlife (mourning rites: tearing garments, sackcloth, weeping, funeral processions). The household chapter's meals coverage is grounded in the excavated four-room/pillared-house plan (a form Stager's own fieldwork helped establish as diagnostic of Israelite settlement): an unroofed central courtyard doubling as the household's working and eating space, with seating on mats/low benches rather than dedicated dining-hall furniture — ordinary households had no separate banqueting-hall architecture.
